newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish president kicks off new government search.
newsitem.headline: Turkish president kicks off new government search.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel on Thursday kicked off a difficult bid to find a new government following the resignation of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, pushed out of office by an army anti-Islamist campaign.
Demirel met main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz, one of the main contenders to fill the prime minister's seat, for an hour of talks at the presidential palace.
"I told him I was ready to take on the responsibility," Yilmaz, head of the conservative Motherland Party, told reporters after the meeting.
The president was to meet three other opposition figures later in the days before nominating a leader who would try to forge a new coalition government from the splintered parliament.
Shares in Istanbul were up 1.28 percent, but trading was expected to remain cautious while uncertainty over the outcome of the talks persisted, brokers said.
Yilmaz's conservative rival Tansu Ciller has been tipped as likely to get the nod from the president, but there were no certainities.
Erbakan quit on Wednesday after months of accusations that he was trying to slowly scrap NATO member Turkey's official secularist system and create an Islamic state similar to Iran.
"Turkey needs a government that can protect the system and make it flourish," said Yilmaz, a former prime minister.
The opposition leader, who has 129 MPs in the 550-seat parliament, could struggle to find coalition allies if Demirel named him as prime minister-designate.
Parliamentary sources said Demirel could appoint a prime minister-designate before the end of the day.
Erbakan stays on as caretaker prime minister for the time being.
He asked the president on Wednesday to give Ciller the task of forming a government so she could set up a coalition that would include the Islamists and head for early elections.
But Demirel, a veteran politician whose post is mostly symbolic, has given no clue as to how he will deal with the government crisis.
Demirel has the power to appoint his own caretaker administration and call elections himself if his appointee fails to come up with a feasible government formula in 45 days.
Erbakan's coalition, set up only a year ago, dissolved in a secularist onslaught led by the secularist generals.
The Turkish press on Thursday quoted unnamed senior military sources as warning that the top brass would closely monitor a new government headed by Ciller that gave the Islamists any government role.
"The (proposed) new government will not be any different from the last one," a leading military official told the Milliyet daily.
The army has openly pledged its readiness to turn back any threat to Turkey's secular order "by force of arms" -- tough talk that has alarmed close NATO ally the United States.

A new government under Ciller would have the support on paper of 282 deputies, enough to pass a confidence vote. But anti-Islamist members of her True Path Party have threatened to abandon her if she does not make a complete break with Erbakan's Welfare Party.
